To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

age, gender and time on dialysis influence T-cell function in healthy volunteers, kidney-transplant patients and dialysis patients and that these factors should be considered in the interpretation of T-cell function as biomarker.
age and gender are important co-factors influencing the expression of biomarkers of T cell function.
the T-cell functions in stable kidney-transplant patient treated with standard immunopressants are decreased as compared to healthy volunteers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of biomarkers for immunosuppressive drug monitoring in the clinical routine.
the identification of co-factors influencing the expression of immunological biomarkers in order to develop a more individualized monitoring of T-cell function.

the identification of co-factors influencing the expression of biomarkers in healthy volunteers, kidney-transplant patients and dialysis patients and may help to understand the mechanisms of action of the immunosuppressive drug therapy in kidney-transplant recipients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
age is a confounding factor for the interpretation of T-cell functions in the three patient populations.
age, gender and disease have an influence on the expression of the biomarkers of T-lymphocyte functions.
age and gender are important factors influencing the expression of T-cell biomarkers, which should be taken into consideration when using T-cell biomarkers in clinical studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
age is the main co-factor influencing the expression of T-cell functions in healthy volunteers and in stable kidney-transplant recipients.

age and gender are important co-factors influencing biomarker expression in healthy volunteers, but in patients on dialysis or kidney-transplant patients other co-factors, e.g. the disease itself and the immunosuppressive treatment, are more important.
the age of the patient is the major factor for T-cell functions, while the gender and the time on dialysis or time after transplantation had no significant effect.
The main takeaway from our work is that
age and gender have a strong impact on T-cell functions in healthy volunteers and patients with chronic kidney disease.
the T-cell functions are significantly lower in kidney-transplant patient than in healthy volunteers and dialyzed patients.
T-cell functions should be interpreted with caution in patients with chronic diseases, such as kidney failure, as they are influenced by co-factors, such as age or gender.
